name: Minocycline foam
lead: Topical minocycline foam is a prescription formulation of the tetracycline antibiotic minocycline, developed to deliver the drug to the skin while limiting systemic exposure. A 4% foam (FMX101) was studied for moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris, and a 1.5% foam (FMX103) for papulopustular rosacea.[1][2]
Phase 3 randomized, vehicle-controlled trials of 12 weeks were run for both conditions.[1][2][3] A pharmacokinetic comparison examined once-daily 4% foam against oral minocycline in acne.[4]

The US FDA approved the 4% foam for acne in 2019 and the 1.5% foam for rosacea in 2020. No looksmaxxing-community material was found for this entry; it appears here because of its use on acne and rosacea.

paras: FMX101 4% was evaluated once daily for 12 weeks in moderate-to-severe acne, with change in inflammatory lesion count and Investigator Global Assessment success as co-primary endpoints.[1][3] Reviews of the product have been published.[5]
FMX103 1.5% was studied for 12 weeks in moderate-to-severe papulopustular rosacea, with the aim of benefiting from topical delivery while minimizing systemic adverse effects.[2]
A study comparing once-daily 4% topical minocycline foam with oral minocycline in acne examined how the two routes differ in drug exposure.[4]

Two identical Phase 3 studies randomized subjects 2:1 to FMX101 4% or vehicle foam for 12 weeks in moderate-to-severe acne.[1] A further 12-week, 1:1 randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 study used the same endpoints.[3] Earlier Phase 2 work in acne and in rosacea preceded these trials.[6]

For rosacea, two 12-week, double-blind, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials of FMX103 1.5% were published together in 2020.[2] Registrations list enrolments of roughly 750 participants each for the two rosacea studies and several hundred to nearly 1,500 for acne trials.[7]

timeline.event: Phase 2 results of topical minocycline foam in acne published.[6]
Phase 3 acne results for FMX101 4% published.[1]
Phase 3 rosacea results for FMX103 1.5% published.[2]

card.summary: Prescription minocycline foam trialled in Phase 3 for acne (4%) and rosacea (1.5%).
card.note: Prescription antibiotic; not an over-the-counter product.

quick.overview:
Topical minocycline foam is a prescription antibiotic foam for acne (4%) and papulopustular rosacea (1.5%).

Both strengths were tested in multiple randomized, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials.
quick.mechanism: It delivers the tetracycline antibiotic minocycline directly to the skin, aiming to limit systemic exposure compared with the oral drug.
quick.risks: Specific adverse-event figures are in the trial reports. It is a prescription antibiotic; oral minocycline is a distinct, systemic product.
